question: How should interpretability broaden when language models can both be objects of explanation and natural-language tools for explaining models and datasets?

key_findings.claim: The paper proposes a two-axis scope: explain an LLM locally or globally, and use an LLM to explain a separate dataset.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1 organizes local generation explanations, global/mechanistic model explanations, and dataset explanations. This usefully distinguishes understanding an LLM from using its language/code interface to analyze tabular or textual data, a category often omitted from narrower mechanistic-interpretability surveys.

key_findings.claim: Natural language and interactivity expand explanatory bandwidth and audience adaptation, but fluency is explicitly not evidence of faithfulness.
key_findings.evidence: The position emphasizes follow-up questions, multiple granularities, multimodal translation, and decomposable tool calls. It simultaneously identifies hallucinated explanations, prompt sensitivity, opacity, model-access constraints, and inference cost as core hazards. The paper cites evidence that chain-of-thought and post-hoc rationales can be plausible yet causally or factually wrong.

key_findings.claim: Interpretation quality should be evaluated by task- and audience-relevant outcomes, not generic human preference for an explanation.
key_findings.evidence: The authors prioritize real-world human studies and human-AI complementarity, note that subjective ratings often fail to predict utility, and describe scalable proxies such as behavioral simulation, synthetic-data tests, ground-truth recovery, faithfulness metrics, and the ability of an interpretation to support model improvement or editing. They also warn that LLM judges can favor their own outputs.

key_findings.claim: The strongest distinctive agenda is LLM-assisted dataset explanation for discovery, not simply asking a model to narrate its own answer.
key_findings.evidence: The survey covers code-based visualization and wrangling, LLM descriptions of interpretable predictive models, LLM-generated features and prompt chains for text data, verified natural-language pattern descriptions, clustering, and topic models. It argues these tools could bridge opaque scientific modalities to human-readable hypotheses, while keeping experiment and expert validation in the loop.

key_findings.claim: The paper is a selective position/review, not an empirical demonstration that LLM explanations improve decisions or discovery.
key_findings.evidence: It introduces no dataset, controlled user study, benchmark, quantitative synthesis, system implementation, or new faithfulness test. Claims about a transformative shift and a possible 'holy grail' are explicitly forward-looking judgments grounded in examples from cited work, not results produced in this paper.

key_findings.claim: Its broad definition risks conflating useful communication, faithful causal explanation, model debugging, and automated data analysis.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines interpretation as extracting relevant knowledge about relationships in a model or data and uses 'interpretable,' 'explainable,' and 'transparent' interchangeably. That inclusiveness enables a unified agenda but makes distinct validity criteria necessary: a helpful visualization, a faithful mechanism, a causal attribution, and a scientifically true hypothesis cannot share one evaluation standard.

method.core_idea: Reorganize LLM interpretability around what is being explained, who consumes it, and whether the LLM is the target or the explanatory interface.
method.mechanism: Synthesize representative literature into local, global/mechanistic, and dataset-explanation categories; identify natural-language/interactivity opportunities; route evaluation toward human utility, faithfulness, behavioral tests, and downstream interventions.
assumptions: Natural language can communicate substantially richer patterns than fixed saliency or feature-importance interfaces.
Grounding, tools, structured workflows, and verification can eventually control hallucinated explanations.
Interpretability should be defined relative to an audience and real decision objective.
LLM capabilities and context length will continue improving enough to support whole-dataset analysis.

techniques.role: Groups attribution, natural-language rationale, chain-of-thought, and retrieval-grounded explanation.
Covers probing, neurons, circuits, data influence, editing, and interactive auditing.
Uses language/code models to visualize, model, describe, cluster, or hypothesize from data.
Judges explanations by improvements to joint real-world outcomes.

evaluations.metric: Conceptual coverage and actionable research priorities
evaluations.result: Proposes reliability, dataset explanation, and interactive explanation as priorities
evaluations.baseline: Narrower surveys centered on explaining individual LLM predictions or internal mechanisms
Cited user studies, faithfulness audits, dataset tools, and mechanistic analyses

limitations: Reviewer-identified: no systematic-review protocol, inclusion criteria, evidence grading, or quantitative meta-analysis is provided.
Reviewer-identified: no original benchmark or human study tests the paper's two recommended research priorities.
Reviewer-identified: treating interpretability, explainability, and transparency interchangeably obscures causal faithfulness versus usability.
Reviewer-identified: the 2024 snapshot predates later reasoning-model monitoring and multimodal explainability results.
Reviewer-identified: proprietary model and training-data access constraints make several global analyses unavailable in the very settings where explanations are most socially consequential.
failure_modes: A fluent interactive system increases user trust while giving post-hoc rationalizations unrelated to model computation.
LLM-as-judge evaluation rewards style, verbosity, or self-generated answers rather than faithfulness.
Dataset explanations amplify training-data priors and produce plausible scientific hypotheses unsupported by the supplied data.
Conversation personalization hides inconsistent answers across users or paraphrases.
Tool-generated charts or statistics are correct but the language narrative misstates them.
High inference and human-audit costs make rigorous interactive evaluation impractical.
reusable_insights: Every explanation artifact should declare its audience, decision objective, evidence source, and intended faithfulness notion.
Interactive explanations should expose auditable intermediate tool calls and permit counterfactual follow-up tests.
Dataset discovery systems need held-out statistical verification and expert review, not self-consistency alone.
Use separate scorecards for causal fidelity, factual grounding, usability, robustness, and human-AI complementarity.
open_questions: What benchmark can test whether interactive explanations improve calibrated human decisions rather than merely satisfaction?
How should a dataset-explanation agent control false-discovery rates across adaptively generated hypotheses?
Can black-box explanations be causally audited without weights, gradients, or training data?
How do explanation needs differ between debugging, regulation, science, medicine, and end-user recourse?
Can interfaces communicate uncertainty and contradictory evidence without overwhelming users?
Which explanation behaviors remain stable across prompts, models, and repeated conversations?

competitive_landscape.title: From Understanding to Utilization: A Survey on Explainability for Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Systematizes local/global explanations, evaluation resources, and downstream uses; the reviewed paper is a shorter position that gives unusual emphasis to LLM-assisted dataset explanation and interaction.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
competitive_landscape.difference: Demonstrates that CoT can conceal input biases and rationalize wrong answers; it supplies concrete evidence for the reviewed paper's warning that natural-language explanation is not automatically faithful.

competitive_landscape.title: TalkToModel: Understanding Machine Learning Models With Open Ended Dialogues
competitive_landscape.difference: Builds and evaluates a conversational interface that calls tabular-model explanation tools; the reviewed paper generalizes this interaction pattern into a broader LLM interpretability priority.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Foundation Models Wrangle Your Data?
competitive_landscape.difference: Empirically studies foundation models for data-wrangling operations; the reviewed paper situates wrangling alongside visualization, interpretable modeling, description, and scientific discovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Transparent AI: A Survey on Explainable Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Organizes newer XAI methods by Transformer architecture and updates resources/applications; the reviewed paper's enduring distinctiveness is its audience-centered interactive and dataset-explanation agenda.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: LLMs can redefine interpretability through expressive natural-language interfaces, especially for interactive explanations and explaining datasets.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The taxonomy and 160-plus cited examples demonstrate breadth and motivate the two priorities, while the paper itself contributes no empirical validation.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The position's most useful novelty is expanding the unit of explanation from a prediction/model to an entire dataset and treating interaction as central. Its claims are an agenda, not evidence that LLM narration is faithful or that discovery systems work reliably.

reviewer_notes: Read all 12 pages, including taxonomy figures, evaluation discussion, dataset-explanation examples, priorities, and references. Current competing surveys and primary empirical faithfulness work were checked on arXiv and NeurIPS on 2026-08-23.
